correctness.rationale: For every prime power q and k>=2 in the q-subspace disjointness graph qK_(2k:k), fixing A, the linear stabilizer acts transitively on U with fixed s=dim(U∩A). The direct-sum/graph description gives |O_s|=q^((k-s)^2)[k choose s]_q^2. Complements W of A are graphs of f:B→A, and W∩U=0 iff the induced restriction D→A/C is bijective (both rank k-s); this counts q^(k^2) product_(j=1)^(k-s)(1-q^(-j)) common neighbours, strictly increasing with s. Round one separates the anchor, all complements, and remaining vertices; round two splits by these common-neighbour counts. k=2 needs only one round, and k>=3 needs two because round one has three classes versus k+1>=4. These are unrestricted algebraic deductions, not inferred from finite test outputs. The actual source Git tree and RESULT.md/check_formula.py/check_refinement.py were inspected; arithmetic formula independently follows from GL rank counting.
